# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/config_reference.py from the Compose files, the launcher, docker/.env.example and the
     application code. Do not edit by hand: change the code or the script's tables, then run
     python3 scripts/config_reference.py. The repository check fails when this page drifts. -->

Flux is configured with environment variables in one private file: `docker/.env` in a source checkout
(`./flux up` creates it from [`docker/.env.example`](../../docker/.env.example) with new secrets) or `.env`
beside a release's `compose.yaml`. Compose reads the file and passes each value to the services that need it.
After a change, apply it with `./flux up` (source) or `docker compose --env-file .env -f compose.yaml up -d --wait`
(release). A variable exported in your shell overrides the file, so do not export Flux variables on a server.
Keep the file private (`chmod 600`) and keep it with your backups: it holds the database password and the
secrets that cannot change.

Each variable lists its type, its default, the services that receive it and where it applies:
**release** is the release `compose.yaml`, **source** the source checkout's Compose file that `./flux` runs,
an **overlay** an optional extra Compose file, and `./flux` the launcher itself. **Override only** means the
application reads it but no shipped Compose file passes it in:
add it under the service's `environment:` in `docker/compose.override.yaml`, which `./flux` includes when it
exists. A wrong value stops the service at start with a message that names the variable.

## Settings you will probably change

- [`FLUX_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`](#flux_public_origin): origin URL
- [`FLUX_SIGNUP`](#flux_signup): `open`, `verified`, `off`
- [`FLUX_SMTP_URL`](#flux_smtp_url): SMTP URL
- [`FLUX_MAIL_FROM`](#flux_mail_from): address
- [`FLUX_TRUSTED_PROXIES`](#flux_trusted_proxies): list of IPs or CIDRs
- [`FLUX_VAPID_SUBJECT`](#flux_vapid_subject): `mailto:` or `https:` URL
- [`FLUX_API_MEMORY`](#flux_api_memory): Compose memory size
- [`FLUX_WORKER_MEMORY`](#flux_worker_memory): Compose memory size

## Instance and network

Where Flux listens and the one address people use. Every deployment sets `FLUX_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`.

### `FLUX_PROJECT`

**Type** name · **Default** generated by `./flux up` (`flux-<directory>-<hash>`); release: `flux` · **Used by** release, `./flux`

Compose project name: prefixes the containers and the `pgdata` and `files` volumes. `./flux` writes `flux-<directory>-<hash of the checkout path>` on first use. Keep it across upgrades, or the new version starts with empty volumes. Example: `flux`.

### `FLUX_PORT`

**Type** port · **Default** `8081` · **Used by** api (release, source, `./flux`)

Port of the API on the host's loopback address (`127.0.0.1`). Point the TLS reverse proxy at it. `./flux up` reads it only when it creates `docker/.env`. Example: `8081`.

### `FLUX_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`

**Type** origin URL · **Default** **required** · **Used by** api, worker (release, source)

The exact origin people open, without a path. It is the only origin accepted for state-changing browser requests, the base of mailed links, OAuth and MCP addresses. `https` makes cookies `Secure`; plain `http` is accepted only for loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`), any other `http` origin stops the API. Example: `https://flux.example.org`.

### `FLUX_TRUSTED_PROXIES`

**Type** list of IPs or CIDRs · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

Comma-separated reverse-proxy addresses whose `X-Forwarded-For` is believed. Empty trusts none, and the socket peer is the client address. Measure the proxy's address as in the [reverse proxy guide](reverse-proxy.md#trust-only-the-measured-proxy-peer); never `0.0.0.0/0`. Example: `172.27.0.1/32`.

## Database

PostgreSQL runs in the `db` service with the `pgdata` volume; it is never published.

### `POSTGRES_USER`

**Type** name · **Default** `flux` · **Used by** api, db, migrate, worker (release, source)

PostgreSQL user, also part of the database URL of every Flux service. Example: `flux`.

### `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`

**Type** secret · **Default** **required** · **Used by** api, db, migrate, worker (release, source)

PostgreSQL password, part of the database URL: use hex (`openssl rand -hex 32`). `./flux up` generates it. Never change it on an existing volume.

### `POSTGRES_DB`

**Type** name · **Default** `flux` · **Used by** api, db, migrate, worker (release, source)

PostgreSQL database name. Example: `flux`.

### `FLUX_DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`

**Type** integer, 100–60000 ms · **Default** `1500` · **Used by** api, worker, migrate (override only)

How long a request waits for a database connection (pool of 10 per process) before it fails.

## Accounts, sign-up and sessions

### `FLUX_AUTH_SECRET`

**Type** secret, ≥ 32 characters · **Default** **required** · **Used by** api (release, source)

Signs session cookies, invite-link tokens and cursors. Changing it signs everyone out and voids pending invite links.

### `FLUX_SIGNUP`

**Type** `open`, `verified`, `off` · **Default** `open` · **Used by** api (release, source)

Who may create a password account. `open`: anyone who reaches Flux. `verified`: anyone who can confirm an address by mail; it proves a mailbox, not membership of your team (needs email; without it sign-up is closed). `off`: nobody, including you, so create your own account first. A provider in `sso` mode closes password sign-up whatever this says, and an invite link never opens closed sign-up. See [who can sign up](install.md#5-decide-who-can-sign-up). Example: `off`.

### `FLUX_PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS`

**Type** integer, 60–86400 s · **Default** `3600` · **Used by** api (release, source)

Lifetime of a password reset link. Links are single use and stored hashed. Example: `3600`.

### `FLUX_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT`

**Type** `true`, `false` · **Default** `true` · **Used by** api (release, source)

In-memory rate limit on sign-in, sign-up and reset. Only the test scripts turn it off. Example: `true`.

## Single sign-on (OpenID Connect)

Optional, one provider. The [single sign-on guide](single-sign-on.md) walks through it.

### `FLUX_OIDC_ISSUER`

**Type** https URL · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

Issuer of the OpenID Connect provider. Set it with `FLUX_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, or neither. Must be `https` (plain `http` only for a loopback issuer). Changing it later makes a new provider: people link again. Example: `https://id.example.org/realms/team`.

### `FLUX_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`

**Type** string · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

Client id registered at the provider. Example: `flux`.

### `FLUX_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_HOST_FILE`

**Type** absolute host path · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (source)

File on the host holding the client secret, mounted read-only into the API at `/run/secrets/flux_oidc_client_secret`. The source Compose file mounts it; with the release `compose.yaml`, mount the file at that path in an override ([how](single-sign-on.md#set-it-up)). Example: `/etc/flux/oidc-client-secret`.

### `FLUX_OIDC_LABEL`

**Type** text, ≤ 60 characters · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

Name on the sign-in button. Empty shows “single sign-on”. Example: `Example ID`.

### `FLUX_SSO_MODE`

**Type** `sso`, `prepare` · **Default** `sso` · **Used by** api (release, source)

`prepare` keeps password sign-in while existing accounts link their provider identity; `sso` is the cutover, after which ordinary sign-in is through the provider only. `prepare` needs a provider. Example: `prepare`.

### `FLUX_OIDC_CONFIRMATION_MAX_AGE`

**Type** duration, `1h`–`30d` · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

How long the provider's last confirmation of a person keeps their access, in whole hours or days. Empty is `7d`. Example: `12h`.

### `FLUX_OIDC_STANDING`

**Type** `refresh`, `off` · **Default** `refresh` · **Used by** api (release, source)

`refresh` checks at the provider that each signed-in person still has an account there; `off` keeps only logout and the confirmation age. Example: `off`.

### `FLUX_OIDC_STANDING_INTERVAL_SECONDS`

**Type** integer, 5–86400 s · **Default** `900` · **Used by** api (release, source)

How often the standing check runs per live identity. Example: `900`.

## Email

Optional. Without it password reset reports unavailable; the in-app Inbox and push keep working.

### `FLUX_SMTP_URL`

**Type** SMTP URL · **Default** empty (`./flux dev`: `smtp://mailpit:1025`) · **Used by** api, worker (release, source, `./flux`)

Transport for password reset and notification email. TLS: `smtps://…:465` or `smtp://…:587?requireTLS=true`; certificates are verified. Percent-encode special characters in the user name and password. Needs `FLUX_MAIL_FROM`. Example: `smtps://flux:password@mail.example.org:465`.

### `FLUX_MAIL_FROM`

**Type** address · **Default** empty (`./flux dev`: `Flux dev <flux-dev@localhost>`) · **Used by** api, worker (release, source, `./flux`)

Sender of every mail. Required when `FLUX_SMTP_URL` is set. Example: `Flux <flux@example.org>`.

## Web Push

Optional, all three or none. See [phones, tablets and push](mobile-and-push.md).

### `FLUX_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`

**Type** base64url P-256 key · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, worker (release, source)

Public VAPID key; the API gives it to browsers. Generate the pair once (`web-push generate-vapid-keys`, see [push](mobile-and-push.md)); `./flux up` does it for a source checkout.

### `FLUX_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** worker (release, source)

Private VAPID key; only the worker receives it. Changing the pair makes every device subscribe again.

### `FLUX_VAPID_SUBJECT`

**Type** `mailto:` or `https:` URL · **Default** empty · **Used by** worker (release, source)

Operator contact sent to the push services. Use a real, reachable address. Example: `mailto:ops@example.org`.

## Collaboration, link cards and the live stream

### `FLUX_LIVE_EDITING`

**Type** `on`, `off` · **Default** `on` · **Used by** api (release, source)

Shared live editing of maps and Wiki pages. `off` keeps the ordinary saved views and editors; save shared working copies before turning it off. Other values stop the API. Example: `off`.

### `FLUX_LINK_PREVIEWS`

**Type** `on`, `off` · **Default** `off` · **Used by** api (release, source)

`on` lets the server fetch the title and description of links in messages for their cards. Only public `http(s)` addresses on default ports; never in encrypted spaces. A fetch tells the site this server's address. Example: `on`.

### `FLUX_STREAM_HEARTBEAT_MS`

**Type** integer, ≥ 100 ms · **Default** `25000` · **Used by** api (release, source)

Ping, session recheck and polling interval of the live WebSocket stream. Keep it below your proxy's idle timeout. Example: `25000`.

## Live media: LiveKit and TURN

Only with the optional overlays `docker/compose.live.yaml` and `docker/compose.live.turn.yaml`, layered on the source Compose file. The release `compose.yaml` does not include live media yet.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_API_KEY`

**Type** string · **Default** **required** · **Used by** api, livekit (live-media overlay, TURN overlay)

LiveKit API key, shared by the API and the SFU. Rotate with the secret. Example: `livekit-key-1`.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_API_SECRET`

**Type** secret · **Default** **required** · **Used by** api, livekit (live-media overlay, TURN overlay)

LiveKit API secret.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_PUBLIC_IP`

**Type** IP address · **Default** **required** · **Used by** livekit (live-media overlay, TURN overlay)

Public media address advertised to browsers in ICE candidates. Example: `203.0.113.20`.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_DOMAIN`

**Type** DNS name · **Default** **required** · **Used by** livekit (live-media overlay)

Operator-owned media name used for STUN and TURN/UDP. Example: `media.example.org`.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_MEDIA_CIDR`

**Type** CIDR · **Default** `0.0.0.0/0` · **Used by** livekit (live-media overlay, TURN overlay)

The SFU's media interface when the host has several; the default keeps every IPv4 interface. Example: `203.0.113.20/32`.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_ICE_TCP_PORT`

**Type** port · **Default** `7881` · **Used by** livekit (live-media overlay)

Host port of ICE over TCP.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_ICE_UDP_PORT`

**Type** port · **Default** `7882` · **Used by** livekit (live-media overlay)

Host port of the ICE UDP mux.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_TURN_UDP_PORT`

**Type** port · **Default** `3478` · **Used by** livekit (live-media overlay)

Host port of TURN/UDP and STUN.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_TURN_DOMAIN`

**Type** DNS name · **Default** **required** · **Used by** livekit (TURN overlay)

Name dedicated to TURN/TLS; the certificate's SAN must match. Example: `turn.example.org`.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_TURN_CERT_DIR`

**Type** absolute host path · **Default** **required** · **Used by** livekit (TURN overlay)

Directory with `fullchain.pem` and `privkey.pem` for the TURN name, readable by the LiveKit container. Example: `/etc/flux/turn-tls`.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_TURN_TLS_BIND`

**Type** IP address · **Default** `0.0.0.0` · **Used by** livekit (TURN overlay)

Address for TURN/TLS on TCP/443. The default conflicts with an HTTPS proxy on the same address: use a dedicated IP. Example: `203.0.113.21`.

### `FLUX_LIVEKIT_TURN_TLS_HOST_PORT`

**Type** port · **Default** `443` · **Used by** livekit (TURN overlay)

Host port of TURN/TLS. Keep 443 for a public deployment.

## AI providers

Owners connect their own AI provider in **Settings → Agents and AI**. These switches decide what the instance allows. They are read by the source checkout's Compose file; the release `compose.yaml` does not pass them yet.

### `FLUX_BACKGROUND_KEY_HOST_FILE`

**Type** absolute host path · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, worker (source)

File with 32 random bytes that seals owners' AI keys for work the worker does on their behalf. Keep it outside the checkout and the database backup. Empty leaves the assistant and background suggestions unavailable. Example: `/etc/flux/background.key`.

### `FLUX_PERSONAL_RUNS`

**Type** empty, `off`, `on` · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, worker (source)

`on` lets owners run their assistant on their own AI connection. Needs `FLUX_BACKGROUND_KEY_HOST_FILE`. Example: `on`.

### `FLUX_BACKGROUND_COMPARISONS`

**Type** empty, `off`, `on` · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, worker (source)

`on` lets owners enable background suggestions, which the worker runs on each owner's own AI connection. Needs `FLUX_BACKGROUND_KEY_HOST_FILE`. Example: `on`.

### `FLUX_AI_PRIVATE_TARGETS`

**Type** list of hosts, IPs or CIDRs · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, worker (source)

Private addresses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint may use, such as a local model server. Empty allows public HTTPS endpoints only; cloud metadata addresses are always refused. Example: `ollama,10.0.0.0/8`.

## Agent runtime: the owner's own Claude Code or Codex

Off by default. See the [agent runtime guide](agent-runtime.md); `./flux ai on` writes these for you.

### `FLUX_AGENT_RUNTIME`

**Type** empty, `claude_code`, `codex`, `claude_code,codex` · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, runtime-1, runtime-2, runtime-3, runtime-4, runtime-egress, runtime-install, worker (release runtime overlay, source, `./flux`)

Lets people sign in with their own Claude or ChatGPT subscription and run that CLI in an isolated slot. Empty is off and no runtime service runs. Example: `codex`.

### `FLUX_AGENT_RUNTIME_COMMERCIAL_TERMS`

**Type** date `YYYY-MM-DD` · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, worker (release runtime overlay, source)

Required with `claude_code`: the date you agreed to Anthropic's Commercial Terms with Anthropic. Recorded, not verified. Example: `2026-10-01`.

### `FLUX_AGENT_RUNTIME_IDLE_DAYS`

**Type** integer, 1–365 days · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, worker (release runtime overlay, source)

Release a slot from its person after this many days without a run. Empty is off. Example: `30`.

### `FLUX_RUNTIME_MANAGER_SECRET`

**Type** secret, ≥ 32 characters · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** api, runtime-manager, worker (release runtime overlay, source)

Authenticates the API and worker to the runtime manager. Generated by `./flux` or `runtime.sh`.

### `FLUX_RUNTIME_SECRET_1`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** runtime-1, runtime-manager (release runtime overlay, source)

Secret of slot `runtime-1`, shared only with the manager.

### `FLUX_RUNTIME_SECRET_2`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** runtime-2, runtime-manager (release runtime overlay, source)

Secret of slot `runtime-2`.

### `FLUX_RUNTIME_SECRET_3`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** runtime-3, runtime-manager (release runtime overlay, source)

Secret of slot `runtime-3`.

### `FLUX_RUNTIME_SECRET_4`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** runtime-4, runtime-manager (release runtime overlay, source)

Secret of slot `runtime-4`. [More slots](agent-runtime.md#more-slots) take `FLUX_RUNTIME_SECRET_<n>` the same way.

### `FLUX_AGENT_RUNTIME_RECONCILE_MS`

**Type** integer, 500–600000 ms · **Default** `10000` · **Used by** worker (override only)

How often the worker reconciles slot bindings with the runtime manager.

## Encrypted spaces and the keyring

See [operating encrypted spaces](encrypted-spaces.md). `./flux up` generates the secrets.

### `FLUX_KEYRING`

**Type** `on`, `off` · **Default** `on` · **Used by** api, worker (release, source)

`off` disables encrypted spaces: each stays locked and none can be created. Example: `off`.

### `FLUX_KEYRING_TOKEN`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** api, keyring, worker (release, source)

Authenticates the API and worker to the keyring on its internal network. Empty leaves the keyring idle and every encrypted space locked.

### `FLUX_KEY_PIN_SECRET`

**Type** secret, ≥ 32 characters · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** api, worker (release, source)

Pins every unlock password and key version, so rows planted in the database are refused. Never change it; back it up with `docker/.env`, not with the database.

### `FLUX_SWAP_ACKNOWLEDGED`

**Type** empty, `encrypted-swap` · **Default** empty · **Used by** api, keyring, worker (release, source)

Declares that every swap device is encrypted with a key not stored on disk. Only then may keys be held where swap is on and not limited per container. Example: `encrypted-swap`.

### `FLUX_SEALED_SEARCH_MAX_BYTES`

**Type** integer, bytes · **Default** `268435456` (256 MiB), at most the process bound · **Used by** api (override only)

Largest in-memory search index of one unlocked encrypted space (estimated heap); a larger space answers that search is unavailable.

### `FLUX_SEALED_SEARCH_PROCESS_MAX_BYTES`

**Type** integer, bytes · **Default** a quarter of the container memory, 64–512 MiB · **Used by** api (override only)

Bound on all encrypted-space search indexes of one API process.

### `FLUX_SEALED_SEARCH_IDLE_MS`

**Type** integer, ms · **Default** `300000` · **Used by** api (override only)

An index nobody searched for this long may be evicted for another space's.

## Memory limits

Memory and swap are limited to the same value, so these containers cannot write memory to a swap device.

### `FLUX_API_MEMORY`

**Type** Compose memory size · **Default** `2g` · **Used by** api (release, source)

Memory of `api` (measured peak 431 MB in the encryption checks). Example: `3g`.

### `FLUX_WORKER_MEMORY`

**Type** Compose memory size · **Default** `1g` · **Used by** worker (release, source)

Memory of `worker` (measured peak 111 MB). Example: `2g`.

### `FLUX_KEYRING_MEMORY`

**Type** Compose memory size · **Default** `128m` · **Used by** keyring (release, source)

Memory of `keyring` (measured peak 42 MB). Example: `256m`.

## GitHub App (optional)

A read-only GitHub App links pull requests to tasks. Set all six secrets together, or none.

### `FLUX_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`

**Type** string · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

The App's OAuth client id.

### `FLUX_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

The App's OAuth client secret. Never give it to agents or models.

### `FLUX_GITHUB_APP_ID`

**Type** integer · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

The App's numeric id.

### `FLUX_GITHUB_APP_SLUG`

**Type** slug · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

The App's URL name (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`). Example: `acme-team-app`.

### `FLUX_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

**Type** secret, ≥ 32 characters · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

Verifies webhook deliveries.

### `FLUX_GITHUB_DELIVERY`

**Type** `webhook`, `poll` · **Default** `webhook` · **Used by** api (release, source)

`poll` when GitHub cannot reach this server: open linked pull requests are read every 2 minutes. Example: `poll`.

### `FLUX_GITHUB_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

**Type** 64 hex characters · **Default** empty · **Used by** api (release, source)

AES key for stored GitHub credentials. Keep it with your backups to reconnect them after a restore.

## Source checkout, launcher and checks

Read by `./flux`, the hot-reload `dev` profile, the release `runtime.sh` or the check scripts, not by the application.

### `FLUX_FIXTURE_TOKEN`

**Type** secret · **Default** **required** (source); release: empty · **Used by** api, keyring, worker (release, source)

Enables the integration-fixture endpoints used by smoke checks, behind this bearer token. The source Compose file requires it and `./flux up` generates it; leave it empty in a release `.env`.

### `FLUX_BACKUP_DIR`

**Type** path · **Default** `backups/` in the checkout · **Used by** `./flux`

Where `./flux backup` writes archives. Example: `/mnt/backup/flux`.

### `FLUX_NO_CACHE`

**Type** `1` · **Default** empty · **Used by** `./flux`

`1` builds the image without the Docker build cache (`./flux up`, `./flux upgrade`). Example: `1`.

### `FLUX_WAIT_TIMEOUT`

**Type** seconds · **Default** `300` · **Used by** `./flux`, `runtime.sh`

How long `./flux` and `runtime.sh` wait for services to become healthy. Example: `600`.

### `FLUX_COWORK_WATCHDOG_SECONDS`

**Type** seconds · **Default** `300` · **Used by** `./flux`

Stops a native `./flux cowork` run after this long. Example: `600`.

### `FLUX_ENV_FILE`

**Type** path · **Default** `.env` beside `runtime.sh` · **Used by** `runtime.sh`

Settings file the release `runtime.sh` reads. Example: `/srv/flux/.env`.

### `FLUX_DEV_PORT`

**Type** port · **Default** `5173` · **Used by** web (dev, `./flux`)

`./flux dev` only: port of the Vite dev server; the dev origin is `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Does nothing on a server.

### `FLUX_DEV_POLL`

**Type** `true`, `false` · **Default** `false` · **Used by** web (dev)

`./flux dev` only: watch files by polling, for file systems without change events. Example: `true`.

### `FLUX_MAILPIT_PORT`

**Type** port · **Default** `8025` · **Used by** source, `./flux`

`./flux dev` and checks: port of the local mail catcher's web page. Does nothing on a server.

### `FLUX_DEMO_OWNER_PASSWORD`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** `./flux`

Password `./flux demo` gives the demo owner. Leave empty on a real deployment and never run the demo there.

### `FLUX_DEMO_PARTNER_PASSWORD`

**Type** secret · **Default** empty; generated by `./flux` · **Used by** `./flux`

Password `./flux demo` gives the second demo account.

## Set by Flux, not by you

The services also read 61 names that Compose, the launcher or the code sets: wiring
between services and test switches. Do not set them. They are listed for developers in
[internal configuration names](../development/configuration-internal.md).

## Launcher commands

`./flux help` in a source checkout prints this list; it is copied here from the launcher. The
[operations overview](README.md) links each command to its guide.

```text
Flux launcher. Flux runs in Docker; the external cowork action also needs the native Codex CLI.

  ./flux up              Create docker/.env with new secrets if it is missing (never overwrites it),
                         build, migrate, start and print the URL.
  ./flux demo [--dev]    Seed demo data through the public API and print two logins.
                         Refuses non-loopback (production-looking) origins unless --force.
  ./flux dev [--build]   Hot-reload development in Docker: Vite for the web app, tsx watch
            [--follow]   for API and worker, PostgreSQL and Mailpit; separate data.
  ./flux down            Stop both stacks; keep data.
  ./flux logs [--dev] [service]   Follow logs (api, worker, web, db, migrate, mailpit).
  ./flux reset [-y]      Delete this checkout's data volumes after confirmation.
  ./flux clean [-y]      reset, plus remove the images this checkout built.
  ./flux backup [--output DIR] [--keep N]
                         Stop API and worker, write a timestamped archive (database dump, files
                         volume, .env, manifest with checksums) to backups/, restart them.
  ./flux restore <archive> [--migrate] [--revoke-agent-connections] [-y]
                         Check the archive, confirm, replace this project's data with it, migrate
                         and run health and schema checks. Refuses another Flux version unless
                         --migrate. --revoke-agent-connections ends every agent connection and
                         OAuth token from the backup (they need connecting again).
  ./flux export <project> [--as EMAIL] [--output FILE]
                         Write a project's JSON-plus-files bundle to exports/ (as the workspace
                         owner by default; the account needs project.manage).
  ./flux identity link <userId> --subject <sub> --reason "<why>" [--old-issuer <URL>] [--allow-sso]
                         Audited operator recovery by Flux account id; requires the running API.
  ./flux identity unlink <userId> --reason "<why>"
                         Audited operator removal of the provider sign-in; refused as the last way in.
  ./flux upgrade [--pull] [-y]
                         Back up, (git pull,) build this checkout, migrate and check health; on
                         failure print the restore instructions.
  ./flux runtime status | release runtime-<n> | purge [-y]
                         Agent runtime (FLUX_AGENT_RUNTIME): show slots and bindings, release one slot's
                         binding (its owner is signed out and told), or sign out and delete every login.
  ./flux ai on           Ask whether people may sign in with their own ChatGPT and Claude subscriptions
                         (Enter = yes for Codex; Claude Code needs a typed y to Anthropic's Commercial
                         Terms), write FLUX_AGENT_RUNTIME into docker/.env and apply it. The first
                         interactive ./flux up asks the same once. Needs a terminal.
  ./flux cowork start|resume --client codex --origin URL --connection ID --project ID
                         Supplied native host action from Connect/Agents. Requires this built checkout,
                         Docker and Codex 0.160.1 signed in with ChatGPT. Resume uses its exact saved thread
                         (unverified with a real account). A native run is stopped after
                         FLUX_COWORK_WATCHDOG_SECONDS (default 300).
  ./flux help            This text.

Commands that start, stop, back up, restore or delete refuse a Compose project that belongs to another
checkout; --force-project overrides that check.

Environment: FLUX_PROJECT (Compose project; default flux-<dir>-<hash of this checkout's path>,
stored in docker/.env on first use; dev uses <project>-dev),
FLUX_PORT (8081, used when creating .env), FLUX_DEV_PORT (5173), FLUX_MAILPIT_PORT (8025),
FLUX_NO_CACHE=1 (build without the Docker cache), FLUX_BACKUP_DIR (default backups/).
Operations guide: docs/operations/README.md.
```
